subject: strandbeest

Category: Abstract.
Subject: wind-walking beach creature of tubes.
Style: Theo Jansen kinetic sculpture.

spec.name: Strandbeest Windwalker
spec.description: A Theo Jansen-style kinetic beach creature: a yellow PVC-tube skeleton with eight Jansen-linkage legs, a rack of pressure bottles for lungs, a tube-and-sail rig on its back, and a sniffing snout with a hinged jaw.
spec.layout: A long, low, spidery walker facing +Z. Sand-dusted rubber feet touch y=0 in two staggered lanes per side: left x=0.95 and 1.12, right x=-0.95 and -1.12. Above them runs a triangular-truss yellow tube frame about 1.4 m wide with a crankshaft across it at y=1.0. On the frame's back half stands a tall rig: a central mast and two spread triangular wing-sails of pale paper on tube ribs, topping out at y=2.4. In front of the mast, over the frame's middle, sits a standing rack of translucent blue pressure bottles with red caps, joined by a manifold of thin tubes. A short neck of tubes curves forward and up to a blocky snout head. It has two big bottle-cap eyes, an upper jaw and a separately hinged lower jaw. A three-segment whip tail with a small red flag trails behind. The style shows on every part. All structure is chunky round PVC tube in yellow, with darker end-sleeves and elbow connectors at each junction. Tiny black cable-tie boxes and silver bolts sit at joints. Nothing is smooth or organic: everything is a straight or gently bent tube, a triangle, a bottle or a sheet. Colours stay bold and flat, like beach plastic in sun.

parts.builds:
The creature's backbone, in yellow PVC tube (tubeYellow) with tubeYellowDark end-sleeves.
- Truss: two lower side rails at x=±0.5, y=0.85, running z=-1.9 to 1.2, plus one upper ridge tube along x=0 at y=1.3. V-shaped cross-braces join the rails to the ridge every 0.4 m. Elbow connector spheres or short sleeves in tubeYellowDark sit at each junction, with tiny sleeveBlack cable-tie boxes and bolt-coloured bolts.
- Crankshaft: a thick bolt/boltDark rod along x through the crankAxis mount, from x=-1.2 to 1.2. It has bearing blocks where it passes the rails. Offset crank-arm discs and short crank pins, one at each of the 8 leg lanes (x=±0.95 and ±1.12 at the hip z values), phased around the shaft (tubeYellowLight discs, bolt pins).
- Details: a rope loop (rope) over the ridge, a tapeTeal tape band at mid-body, and sandDust stains on the lower rails.
- Joints: the crank joint carries the shaft and discs, and the body joint carries the truss. It must not build legs, bottles, mast or head.
parts.attaches: Hip pins sit at the crank axis lanes (hipL1..hipR4 mounts). frameFront (neckBase) takes the neck; rackBase and mastBase stand on its ridge; frameRear (tailBase) takes the tail.

parts.builds:
Eight Jansen-linkage legs, four per side, in staggered lanes (L1, L3 at x=0.95; L2, L4 at x=1.12; right side mirrored with opposite phase).
- Each leg is a chain hip → knee → foot built from the joint positions. Thick yellow tubes (tubeYellow, radius about 0.03–0.035) run hip→knee and knee→foot. Each has a parallel twin tube offset 0.07 m outward in x, so the leg reads as a flat linkage plate.
- Jansen-style triangulation: a thin upper triangle brace from hip to a point on the thigh, and a short tubeYellowLight strut parallel to the shin. Cross-pegs (bolt, boltDark) and tubeYellowDark sleeves sit at the hip, knee and mid-shin joints, with sleeveBlack cable ties.
- Feet: each foot is a chunky rubberFoot pad (flattened capsule or box with a rounded toe) whose bottom touches y=0. A thin wetSand band sits on top of the pad and a sandDust smear on the shin ends. The foot rides footXn, the shin rides kneeXn and the thigh rides hipXn.
- No frame or crank geometry. Legs stay in this neutral rest pose, spread out, and clear one another in z and x lanes.
parts.attaches: Each hip meets the crank-disc pin at its hipXn mount on the frame (x=±0.95 or ±1.12, y=1.0). Feet rest on the floorLine (y=0).

parts.builds:
The wind-pressure bottle rack standing on the frame's ridge and rails, between z=-0.3 and 1.15, riding the body joint.
- Bottles: about 10–12 upright translucent bottleBlue PET bottles, each about 0.55 m tall and 0.16 m across, with a faceted body, a tapered shoulder, a neck and a capRed cap. Each has a bottleBlueDark base ring and a lighter highlight stripe. They stand in two staggered rows across x=±0.65. A few have tapeTeal label bands.
- Rack: a tubeYellow base frame of two long rails and cross-rails at y≈1.38, and an upper tubeYellow ring-rack at y≈1.85 holding the bottles, with sleeveBlack cable-tie boxes.
- Manifold: thin tubeYellowDark tubes with T-junctions run along the cap row at y≈2.0 and down to a central valve block (boltDark with bolt knob). Short hoses link neighbouring bottles.
- Pumps: two slim piston rods (bolt) with tubeYellowDark cylinders at the sides of the rack, angled toward the frame.
- Details: a rope tie, a tiny sandDust dusting on the bottle bottoms, and one patch of sailPatch tape. No mast, sail or head.
parts.attaches: Base rails sit on the frame's ridge at the rackBase mount [0,1.35,0.4]. The rack's front end stays behind frameFront (z<1.2); its rear end leaves room for the mast at mastBase (z=-1.0).

parts.builds:
The neck and sniffing snout head at the front, on joints neck1, neck2, head and jaw.
- Neck: a curved chain of yellow tubes (tubeYellow) rising from the neckBase mount at [0,1.2,1.2] to the head at [0,1.45,1.75]. It has two tubeYellowDark sleeves, an elbow sphere, a pair of cable-tie boxes and a bolt at each joint. A thin rope runs along the top.
- Head: a blocky boxy skull made of a yellow tube frame with sailWhite paper panels on the cheeks. An upper snout of tubeYellow, tapering toward z=2.2, has a tubeYellowDark nose-ring at the tip and two nostril-tube stubs in sleeveBlack.
- Eyes: two large bottle-cap eyes, one each side at x=±0.2, y≈1.62, z≈1.9. Each has a capRed ring, an eyeWhite disc, an eyeGlow iris and a pupil dot, plus a bolt bridge between the eyes. Two short tube eyebrows or antennae stick up and forward.
- Jaw: a separate lower jaw hinged on the jaw joint at [0,1.35,1.85]. It is a U of tubeYellow with a mouthInside strip, a few small peg teeth in cableTie colour on both jaws, and a sleeveBlack hinge pin at x=±0.25.
- Rest pose: the jaw is slightly open.
- No frame, legs or sails.
parts.attaches: neck1 starts at neckBase / frameFront [0,1.2,1.2], where the frame's ridge ends. The snout tip reaches snoutTip [0,1.45,2.2].

parts.builds:
The rear sail rig and the whip tail, on joints mast, wingL1/L2, wingR1/R2 and tail1..3.
- Mast: a tall central tubeYellow mast from the mastBase mount [0,1.35,-1.0] to y=2.4, with a tubeYellowDark collar, rope stays down to the frame rails at z≈-1.6 and z≈-0.4, and a small cap sphere on top.
- Wings: two spread wing-sails, left and right, built as membranes or extruded triangular sheets of sailWhite paper. Each spans from the mast out to x≈±1.3 (up to y≈2.2) and down toward y≈1.5 at the back edge. Each sits on a yellow tube rib frame: a leading-edge tube along the wing joints, 4 radial battens, and a trailing tube, with a scalloped trailing edge.
- Sail details: sailSeam strips along the ribs, one or two sailPatch (mustard) patches and a tapeTeal repair strip. A few sleeveBlack cable ties and bolt pins hold the sheet to the tubes, and cableTie colour loops at the corners.
- Tail: three tapering yellow tube segments (tail1, tail2, tail3) curving up and back to z≈-2.4, with sleeves. A small capRed flag or windsock triangle sits at the tip, with a short rope. The model's rearmost point is z=-2.2 (flag tip and tail end must not exceed it).
- No bottles, legs or head.
parts.attaches: The mast base stands on the frame ridge at mastBase [0,1.35,-1.0]. The rack's rear end stays in front (z>-0.3). The tail starts at tailBase / frameRear [0,1.15,-1.9].

calls.reasoning:
I'm sketching out the design for a Theo Jansen-style wind-walking beach creature made of yellow PVC tubes, with sails, Jansen linkage legs, a crank shaft, and pressure bottles, working out proportions like width, height, and length to feel realistic in scale.

Now I'm planning the skeleton: a body root with a crankshaft hinge driving multiple leg modules (each with hip, knee, foot joints) arranged in pairs, plus a front neck/head section with a jaw-like sensing mechanism inspired by how Jansen's creatures probe sand and water, keeping total joint count within limits.

Adding a rotating crank joint with arms, and placing legs as paired parallel plates offset slightly from center on left/right sides. For the upper body I'm planning rear wing sails with cloth stretched on tube frames, hinged at "sailL"/"sailR" with a central mast near the back, keeping overall width under the 2.6 limit.

For the front I'm chaining a neck of three joints into a head with a jaw, adding a tube snout with bottle-shaped eyes mimicking Jansen's pressure-bottle sensors, and placing rows of translucent bottles along the back as a "lungs" component with manifold tubing. I'm also adding a tail chain of three joints holding a wind vane or flag at the end.

Now I'm settling the five main parts -- frame, legs, lungs, head, and sails-plus-tail -- and balancing their cost budget to total under 900. I'm working out the body's bounding geometry and placing the frame box, then positioning the neck and head boxes forward and upward from the body.

Next I'm sketching leg geometry and hip placement, deciding the crank shaft runs along the x-axis through the body with hinge joints at the body's y-level, and spacing the leg attachment points along the z-axis.

Still writing leg joint coordinates...

Still getting collisions between legs at matching knee positions, so I'm trying to stagger the x-lanes instead — putting L1/L3 at one x offset and L2/L4 at another to keep the legs from overlapping on the same side.

Checking the remaining knee offsets on each side to keep the alternating stagger consistent, then setting foot z slightly offset from hip z per side. I'm also working out approximate direction vectors from hip to knee for each leg and confirming the joint parenting hierarchy: body to hip to knee to foot.

Now I'm defining the crank hinge joint on the body and attaching the leg hips at crank axis offsets, plus laying out the spine, neck, head, and jaw joints with their positions and directions, adjusting the neck length and head box sizing as I go.

Adjusting the neck and head box coordinates so the frame tube, neck, and head geometry fit together without overlapping badly, then starting on the tail segment positions.

Now I'm figuring out the sail/mast rigging at the rear: placing the mast joint, wing segments extending outward and upward, and sizing the sail bounding box to match the overall body length.

I realize this overlaps with where the lung bottle bank sits along the back, so I need to reposition the lungs—maybe to the sides or underside—to avoid conflicting with the sail geometry.

I'm arranging ten standing bottles in two rows of five across the rack, and considering simple touches like amber glow lens caps for the eyes while keeping the palette otherwise flat and skipping extra gauges or glow beads to avoid clutter.

Now I'm mapping out mount points for the crank base, mast, tail, and rack, then working through the Jansen-style frame geometry—side rails, hip joints, and the truss connecting lower and upper rails that the crank shaft will pass through.

Now I'm fleshing out the full color palette — yellow conduit, white sail with tinted bottle floats, black and white cable ties, sand tones, red bottle caps, rope, teal tape, metal bolts, rubber feet, and expressive eye/mouth colors for character — settling on roughly twenty hues total, keeping the overall style true to Jansen's kinetic strandbeest aesthetic.

Working out the joint hierarchy next: legs, neck segments (neck1, neck2, head, jaw), tail, mast, and wing joints, totaling around 38 joints. I'm calculating the directional vectors for each leg segment — hip, knee, and foot — to define how the limbs articulate.

Computing mirrored leg directions...

Finishing R4's hip/knee direction vectors the same way, then noting the foot pad should sit with its tube resting at y=0 for ground contact. I'm thinking through the "leg" role for joint naming, then sketching out a part budget allocation across frame, legs, lungs, head, and sails.
